findings.title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions are fire-and-forget and may never run before the request completes
findings.body: In the allRemainingBookings branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` uses an async callback inside forEach. Nothing awaits these promises: `apiDeletes` is later consumed via `await apiDeletes;` (line 617), which awaits a plain array (a no-op), and `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 can run before the async forEach bodies have pushed anything (the first `await getCalendar(credential)` yields before any deleteEvent is pushed). Consequence: when cancelling all remaining recurring bookings, external calendar events may not be deleted at all, or deleted after the response/DB cleanup, and any failures surface as unhandled promise rejections. Replace with `for...of`/`Promise.all` and actually await the resulting promises.

findings.title: forEach(async ...) swallows the returned promises, so deletions are unawaited and errors escape the try/catch
findings.body: The loop `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` discards the promises returned by the async callbacks. Because the callback is now async (it was made async by this PR to await getCalendar), the surrounding try/catch can no longer catch errors thrown while resolving the app import or getCalendar — any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection, and Reschedule() can return before calendar/video events are actually deleted. The identical pattern exists in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125 and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553. Collect the promises (e.g. `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`) so they are awaited and errors are handled.

findings.title: Async forEach callback results discarded; deletion errors become unhandled rejections
findings.body: Same issue as vital/lib/reschedule.ts: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` fire-and-forgets the async work. Previously getCalendar was synchronous, so sync errors were caught by the enclosing try/catch; after this change, rejections from the dynamic import or getCalendar escape the try/catch as unhandled promise rejections, and the function proceeds to send the reschedule email and return `true` regardless of whether calendar/video events were actually deleted. Await the collected promises instead.

findings.title: All dynamic imports are started eagerly at module evaluation; failed chunk loads produce unhandled rejections
findings.body: The appStore object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")` (and all others) at module-evaluation time, so merely importing `@calcom/app-store` kicks off loading every app chunk immediately — the lazy-loading benefit only applies to bundling, not to runtime loading, and on the server every app module is still loaded whenever app-store is imported. Additionally, if any of these top-level import promises rejects (e.g. a broken app build), it becomes an unhandled promise rejection that can crash the Node process even for code paths that never use that app. Wrap the entries in functions/thunks (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) or attach a rejection handler so failures are surfaced only to the code that awaits them.

findings.title: `await apiDeletes` awaits an array, not a promise — deletion failures are silently ignored on paid-booking cancellation
findings.body: In the paid-booking branch, `await apiDeletes;` awaits a plain Array (which resolves immediately), so none of the calendar/video deletion promises pushed into apiDeletes are actually awaited before returning "Booking successfully cancelled.". Combined with this PR's change to push into apiDeletes from an async forEach callback (line 460-470), deletions may not even have been started yet. Use `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)` so integration deletions complete (and failures are observed) before responding.
